thread:
alex_support: FYI customer hit corrupted structured output when using streaming + structured_mode. They see JSON fragments merged across requests. Raised as P1.
ben_runtime: Can you paste the exact failing output and request_id? Also which model variant and cache settings?
alex_support: request_id=rid_0x9b3f. Model: rwd-13b-v1, structured_mode=true, stream=true, use_kv_cache=true (default ttl=60s). Customer says it only happens under sustained parallel traffic (50-200 qps) with batching enabled.
priya_ml: Interesting. Any auth/billing spikes? Retries can cause interleaving if fragments are not isolated.
megan_cs: Customer reported they saw a few 429s earlier today then retried. They did use client-side retry policy with exponential backoff.
alex_support: Here's minimal repro curl (customer sanitized):
```
curl -N -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-***" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-13b-v1","structured_mode":true,"stream":true,"input":"{\"id\":123}\n","max_tokens":256,"batch":true}'
```
They streamed five concurrent requests and occasionally got this response (stream fragments concatenated):
```
{"id":123,"result":{"items":[{"type":"text","value":"hello"}]}}{"id":124,"result":{"items":[{"type":"text","value":"wo"
```
Then later:
```
"rld"}}  <-- fragments from different responses stuck together, causing parser errors
```
ben_runtime: That looks like tokenstream-stitching: fragments from different sessions ended up in the same chunk. Could be race in the batching handoff where KV prefix cache eviction occurs while a batch is being assembled. When cache returns partial prefix + a batch includes stale pointers, the stream boundaries can be mis-ordered.
priya_ml: Also check whether the streaming buffer boundary aligns with our chunk framing. If a batch completion writes directly to the same stream buffer without per-request separators, retries could interleave.
megan_cs: Customer wants an ETA. They called this a blocker for production.
ben_runtime: Immediate mitigation: tell them to set "use_kv_cache":false or use non-streaming mode (stream=false) to avoid fragment joins. Also ask them to disable client retries for a short window while we triage.
alex_support: I sent that as workaround. They confirmed disabling cache reduced incidents but didn't fully eliminate it.
ben_runtime: OK. Assign to eng-runtime. Priya, can you reproduce with a harness that simulates: parallel streaming requests, kv_cache ttl=1s, small batch window (10ms), and client retries enabled? If reproduced, we can add sequence stamping to stream chunks to keep fragments separate.
priya_ml: On it. I'll try to build a repro that toggles cache eviction timing. Hypothesis: eviction callback races with batch flush leading to pointer reuse. I'll instrument with extra logging: batch_id, stream_seq, cache_version.
deploy_bot: deploy scheduled: runtime/patch/stream-frag-logging -> canary in us-west-2 at 1714568200
ben_runtime: Once we have repro, plan is: 1) add per-request stream delimiter header in runtime output, 2) harden cache eviction to wait for inflight batches, 3) add quick hotfix to disable pointer reuse across flush.
megan_cs: I'll keep customer updated. Please paste repro artifacts and decide whether we need a rollback or hotfix.
alex_support: Customer supplied a gzipped tcpdump and sample logs. I uploaded to the incident S3 and shared link in DM.
priya_ml: First repro attempt: I could reproduce a single interleaved chunk within 90 seconds by simulating client retries with 100ms jitter. Will push logs to the shared folder.
ben_runtime: Nice. Prioritizing a short-term fix: add stream chunk metadata (request_id + seq) so clients can detect and drop mixed fragments. Long-term: fix batching handoff. I'll open an internal task and tag eng-runtime and eng-ml.
alex_support: Thanks. For support message cadence: I told customer we'll provide an interim detection header within 24h and a permanent fix next week. They accepted.
megan_cs: Customer impact: production traffic ~400k tokens/day, they asked for credits for errors; finance copy needed if we give credits.
ben_runtime: Keep me posted. If we need a faster rollback, roll back the batching heuristic in us-west canary. For now, set a guardrail: reduce max_batch_size for rwd-13b-v1 to 8 in canary.
alex_support: Noted. I'll update thread when deploy_bot reports canary status.
